name: The Home Depot, Inc.
business: Home Depot sells building materials, home improvement products, tools and installation services to do-it-yourself consumers and professional contractors through stores, branches and online.

events.what: Acquisition of GMS (specialty building products distributor) by SRS closed; margin dilutive (about 20 bps of operating margin pro forma per Bastek, doc 46347); no Item 2.01 or 1.01 8-K returned

CEO Ted Decker on temporary medical leave; CFO Richard McPhail interim principal executive officer, Ann-Marie Campbell oversees operations, Gregory Brenneman chairs the board. Not a reset: no permanent change filed since (latest 5.02 is a 2026-08-21 portfolio expansion for Bastek, Broggi and McPhail, 0000354950-26-000148)

next_event.source: No 2026 investor conference found in Baba; the last was 2025-12-09 (document_id 49190). The CFO said the company looks forward to Decker's return in a few months (Q2 fiscal 2026 call, 2026-08-18, document_id 141486). Fiscal 2027 guidance would come with the Q4 fiscal 2026 call, date not sourced.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: No multi-year margin target. The only numeric margin statement is the one-year fiscal 2026 guide of adjusted operating margin about 12.8% to 13.0% (GAAP 12.4% to 12.6%), BELOW the 13.1% fiscal 2025 actual (doc 46344). The December 2025 investor conference gave a recovery-case sales target (5% to 6% total growth) and only qualitative margin language: operating profit dollars to grow faster than sales once housing recovers. HD fiscal year ends late January or early February; Baba FY-2027 = HD fiscal 2026.

statements.quote: Once we see recovery, we expect to drive operating profit dollars faster than sales, balancing benefits from productivity and leverage between reinvestment in the business and operating profit dollar growth. We will target mid to high single-digit adjusted EPS growth.
statements.speaker: Richard McPhail

statements.quote: In a 2% comp scenario, we would expect to see deleverage and acquisition mix impact of approximately 20 basis points offset by productivity of 20 basis points, resulting in an adjusted operating margin of approximately 13% and adjusted EPS growth of approximately 4%.
statements.speaker: Richard McPhail

statements.quote: Further, we expect operating margin of approximately 12.4%-12.6% and adjusted operating margin of approximately 12.8%-13%.
statements.speaker: Richard McPhail
statements.doc_title: THE HOME DEPOT, INC. Q2 2027 Earnings Call (Baba label; HD fiscal Q2 2026)

street.gap_assumption: Baba labels: FY2026 = HD fiscal 2025 (actual), FY2027 = fiscal 2026, FY2028 = fiscal 2027. No stated margin level, so no gap. Street EBITDA margin is flat (14.67% to 14.83% over three years), consistent with management's own flat-to-down guide; 4-month EBITDA revision +0.3% (stabilized).
street.source: Baba data_financials summary consensus (Visible Alpha), fetched 2026-10-01

evidence_of_progress.note: Order [Q1 fiscal 2026, Q2 fiscal 2026]. Q1 is EBITDA margin from Baba VA actuals (13.94% vs 14.88%); Q2 is GAAP operating margin per CFO (14.3% vs 14.5%; adjusted 14.7% vs 14.8%), helped by a $685M IEEPA tariff refund in COGS. Q2 actuals are not yet loaded in Baba VA, so LTM EBITDA uses Q2 fiscal 2025 to Q1 fiscal 2026. GMS adds mix dilution.

verdict: Not a GXO setup: a cheap mega-cap waiting on a housing recovery, with no numeric margin target, a margin-dilutive GMS deal, and a CEO on temporary medical leave rather than a reset.
open_questions: Does Decker return as planned, or does the board file a permanent CEO change (that would turn B into a live catalyst)?
Will the next investor conference attach a margin number or year to the recovery case's 'operating profit faster than sales'?
How much of the fiscal 2026 margin guide depends on the $685M tariff refund offsetting fuel, freight and input inflation?
